citation: Illinois State Archives, Illinois Public Domain Land Tract Sales Database (Springfield: Office of the Secretary of State).
date: database of the federal land office registers
note: The Archives' index to the sales registers of the federal land offices. Each row carries the purchaser as the register wrote it, the purchaser's stated residence (a COUNTY, and most often UNKNOWN), the aliquot part or town lot, section, township, range, meridian, county, acres, price per acre, total price, type of sale, date of purchase, and the register volume and page. This project read it for seven townships of the third principal meridian through 31 December 1836: T39N R14E and T40N R14E, the two the town stands on (T-0557), all seventy-two of whose sections were read WHOLE (T-0675), and the five that ring them — T39N R13E, T38N R14E, T38N R15E, T40N R13E and T41N R14E (T-0676). Two hundred and fifty-two section queries in all. The database's own search shows at most 150 rows at a time, which is why the reading is by section; the results page's `More` button is a keyset cursor that returns the rows after the last one shown, and following it is what closed the three sections T-0557 had to declare truncated. The ring sweep ran before the cursor was known and stopped at the first page of each section, so one section — T39N R13E 16 — is still held as a first page rather than a section and is not declared read (T-0682). See data/research/land_sales/README.md. The site refuses this runner's datacentre address outright (403 or no route at all, from every user agent), so the pages were fetched through the public r.jina.ai reader, which returns the origin's own HTML — the access route is recorded on every record's locator and changes nothing about what the page says.
